refnamediv.refpurpose: Approximates the Ant notion of a fileset

refsection.title: Introduction
refsection.para: This step selects files using a vocabulary based on the FileSet vocabulary of Ant.

refsection.title: Errors
refsection.para: Errors from the entry body are summarized here.

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: This step is based on the Ant notion of FileSets. Conceptually, all of the files below some starting point (the path) are filtered through a set of inclusions and exclusions. Any files that satisfy the filters are further subjected to a set of selectors (which may use mappers) to determine if they are in the final result or not.
The cx:fileset step differs from Ant in some ways:

listitem.para: The files selected by cx:fileset are normalized with urify(). They exclusively use “/” as the path separator.
The step is only concerned with selecting existing files.
Attributes related to filtering directories are not provided.
It doesn’t support anything like Ant FilterSets which change the contents of files.
The names of the elements and attributes have been changed to make them more consistent with XProc (“compound-name” instead of “compoundname”).
You can’t provide a custom filter or mapper class, the step isn’t extensible in that way.

Ant has a number of features for defining filters, patterns, and selectors and then reusing them by reference. XProc has lots of features for constructing XML documents, so those mechanisms are not supported.

refsection.para: In order to avoid having all of Ant become a dependency, this is a reimplementation of the functionality. The Ant documentation isn’t especially precise. It’s possible that there are unintentional semantic differences beyond the differences outlined here. (Please report them.)
This step differs substantially from he p:directory-list step in that the include and exclude filters are “globs” not regular expressions!
If the source port is not empty, it must contain a fileset document. It is a dynamic error if the source document is not a fileset document.

important.para: Where regular expressions are used, they use the regular expression syntax of the underlying platform. This will change in the future and the XPath regular expression syntax will be used instead. For most simple cases, there’s no difference.

refsection.title: Step options
refsection.para: The cx:fileset step has several options.

listitem.para: The path. The value provided will be normalized with the urify() function. The resulting URI must be a “file” URI. It is a dynamic error if the path provided is not a file: URI.
Several selectors support case-sensitive or case-insensitive comparisons. This option provides the default value for those selectors.
If this option is true, the default exclusions are automatically used.
If this option is true, detailed information will be provided about each file. See p:directory-list for more details.

para.error: It is a dynamic error if the path provided does not exist and error-on-missing-dir is true.

listitem.para: A space or comma separated list of globs. Any file that matches will be excluded.
Several selectors have an option to follow symbolic links. This option provides the default value for those selectors.
A space or comma separated list of globs. Any file that matches will be included, unless it also matches an exclusion. If no inclusions are provided, all of the descendants are included by default.

refsection.title: The fileset document
refsection.para: The fileset document contains zero or more include or exclude elements and zero or more selectors. Some selectors may contain mappers.
A selector tests each file that is filtered through the includes and excludes. If the file “passes” the selection test, it remains included. If it “fails”, it is removed.
Selectors that compare the file in question against other files on the filesystem may use mappers to transform the filename. For example:

This fileset begins with all of the SVG files under /path/to/input. For each one, the present selector tests, does this file exist at an equivalent location under the /path/to/output directory? The glob-mapper changes the .svg extension to .png.
Suppose /path/to/input contains a.svg, b.svg, and c.svg and /path/to/output contains a.svg, b.png, and d.png.

The only file returned will be b.svg. Neither a.svg nor c.svg will be returned because there’s no equivalent PNG file in the output directory. And d.svg won’t be returned because there’s no such file in the input directory.
If more than one selector is provided, that is the same as a single and selector containing all of them.

refsection.title: The fileset element
refsection.para: The fileset element contains the configuration of the step.

The options for default exclusions, case sensitivity, whether it’s an error if the path is missing, and the default for following symbolic links must be specified either on the step or on the fileset element. It is a dynamic error if they are specified in both places. If inclusions or exclusions are specified in both places, both sets of patterns (and the patterns from any nested include or exclude elements) are used.

refsection.title: The include element
refsection.para: The include element identifies a (single) glob pattern to include. If the if attribute is false or the unless attribute is true, the element is ignored.

refsection.title: The exclude element
refsection.para: The exclude element identifies a (single) glob pattern to exclude. If the if attribute is false or the unless attribute is true, the element is ignored.

refsection.title: The contains element
refsection.para: The contains element selects a file if it contains the specified text.
If ignore-whitespace is true, all white space is stripped from the search text and the file before making the comparision.

refsection.title: The content-type element
refsection.para: The content-type element selects a file if it has one of the specified content types.
This selector is not present in Ant.

refsection.title: The date element
refsection.para: The date element selects a file if it’s last modified time matches the constraints specified.
If when is “before”, the last modified time must be before the specified date-time. If it’s “after”, it must be after. If it’s “equal” (the default), it must be equal.

For the purposes of comparision, the last modified time is equal to the specified date time if it’s within granularity milliseconds of the specified date-time. On Windows, the default granularity is 2 seconds, on other systems, it’s 0.

refsection.title: The depend element
refsection.para: The depend element selects a file if it exists under the target-dir and if the target file is newer.

For the purposes of comparision, two files are considered to have the same last modified time if they are within granularity milliseconds of each other. On Windows, the default granularity is 2 seconds, on other systems, it’s 0.
If no mapper is specified, the identity-mapper is used.

refsection.title: The depth element
refsection.para: The depth element selects a file if it is at least min directory levels and at most max directory levels from the root.
If min is unspecified, it defaults to 0. If max is unspecified, it defaults to ∞.

refsection.title: The different element
refsection.para: The different element selects a file if it exists under the target-dir and is different.
The default value for ignore-file-times is true; the default value for ignore-contents is false.

For the purposes of comparision, two files are considered to have the same last modified time if they are within granularity milliseconds of each other. On Windows, the default granularity is 2 seconds, on other systems, it’s 0.
If no mapper is specified, the identity-mapper is used.

refsection.title: The filename element
refsection.para: The filename element matches a file if it matches the glob or regular expression provided.
Exactly one of name or regex must be provided.
This element is like the include element, but it can be combined with other selectors. If negate is true, this element is like the exclude element.

refsection.title: The present element
refsection.para: The present element selects a file by comparing it against an equivalent file under the target-dir.

If present is “srconly”, the file is selected if it only exists in the source (if it is not under the target-dir). If present is “both”, the file is selected if it exists in both places. (A “target only” value is incoherent because the comparison is always against a file that does exist.)
If no mapper is specified, the identity-mapper is used.

refsection.title: The contains-regexp element
refsection.para: The contains-regexp element selects a file if it contains the specified regular expression.
If multi-line is true, the match may extend across line breaks.
If single-line is true, “.” may match newlines. (This is the “dotall” flag in Java regular expressions.

refsection.title: The size element
refsection.para: The size element selects a file based on its size.

If no units are specified, the value is an exact number of bytes. If units are specified, they have the following effect: da multiplies the value by 10, h multiplies the value by 100, k, 1,000, M, 1,000,000, G, 109 T, 1012 and P, 1015.
The remaining units multiply by powers of two: Ki, 1024, Mi, 10242, Gi, 10243, Ti, 10244, and Pi, 10245.
The when attribute determines how the actual file size must compare to the specified value.

refsection.title: The readable element
refsection.para: The readable element selects a file if it is readable by the user.

refsection.title: The writable element
refsection.para: The readable element selects a file if it is writable by the user.

refsection.title: The executable element
refsection.para: The executable element selects a file if it is executable by the user.

refsection.title: The symlink element
refsection.para: The symlink element selects a file if it is a symbolic link.
Symbolic links are platform specific. This selector returns true if the underlying JVM considers a file on the particular filesystem in use a “symbolic link”.

refsection.title: The owned-by element
refsection.para: The owned-by element selects files that are owned by owner.
If the file being tested is a symbolic link and follow-symlinks is true, the ownership of the file linked to is tested. Otherwise the owner of the link is tested.

refsection.title: The posix-group element
refsection.para: The posix-group element selects files that are members of the specified group.
If the file being tested is a symbolic link and follow-symlinks is true, the group of the file linked to is tested. Otherwise the group of the link is tested.
This selector requires a POSIX compatible filesystem. It will always return false in other cases, for example, on Windows.

refsection.title: The posix-permissions element
refsection.para: The posix-permissions element selects files that have specific permissions.
Permissions can be expressed as an octal number (“755”) or using the r/w/- notation (“rwxr-xr-x”). In either case, the match is exact. The selector doesn’t support any kind of wildcard matching.
If the file being tested is a symbolic link and follow-symlinks is true, the permissions of the file linked to are tested. Otherwise the permissions of the link are tested.
This selector requires a POSIX compatible filesystem. It will always return false in other cases, for example, on Windows.

refsection.title: The chained-mapper element
refsection.para: The chained-mapper returns the result of applying each mapper in turn. The initial file is the input to the first mapper, the output from the first mapper is the input to the second mapper, and so on.

refsection.title: The composite-mapper element
refsection.para: The composite-mapper returns the result of applying the (same) initial file to each mapper. This is the union of all the mapper outputs.

refsection.title: The cut-dirs-mapper element
refsection.para: The cut-dirs-mapper removes dirs path segments from the front of the file. If the file has fewer path segments, nothing is returned.

refsection.title: The first-match-mapper element
refsection.para: The first-match-mapper applies the original file to each mapper in turn, returning the results of the first mapper that succeeds.

refsection.title: The flatten-mapper element
refsection.para: The flatten-mapper returns the filename of the original file with all leading path segments removed.

refsection.title: The glob-mapper element
refsection.para: The glob-mapper matches the original file against the from glob. If it doesn’t match, nothing is returned. If it does match, the to glob is used to change the file.
The from and to globs much each contain exactly one *. The text matched by the * in the from glob is used to replace the * in the to glob.

refsection.title: The identity-mapper element
refsection.para: The identity-mapper returns the original file unchanged.

refsection.title: The merge-mapper element
refsection.para: The merge-mapper returns the to value irrespective of the original file.

refsection.title: The package-mapper element
refsection.para: The package-mapper applies the same processing as the regexp-matcher, then replaces all of the “/” characters with “.”.
This turns, for example, org/example/package/Class.java into org.example.package.Class.html assuming the from value is “*.java” and the two value is “*.html”.

refsection.title: The unpackage-mapper element
refsection.para: The unpackage-mapper applies the same processing as the regexp-matcher, then replaces all but the last “.” characters with “/”.
This is the reverse of the package-mapper.

refsection.title: The regexp-mapper element
refsection.para: The regexp-mapper matches the original file against the from regular expression. If it doesn’t match, nothing is returned. If it does match, the to expression is used to change the file.
Each occurrence of “\0” to “\9” is replaced with the corresponding match group from the from expression (where “\0” is the whole string, “\1” is the first match group, etc.

refsection.title: Default exclusions
refsection.para: The default exclusions are:

Any file or directory named .DSStore, .bzr, .bzrignore, .cvsignore, .git, .gitattributes, .gitignore, .gitmodules, .hg, .hgignore, .hgsub, .hgsubstate, .hgtags, .svn, CVS, SCCS, vssver.scc. If a directory name is excluded, so are all of its descendants.
Any file with a name that ends with ~.
Any file with a name that starts with .# or ._.
Any file with a name that begins and ends with # or begins and ends with %.

refsection.title: Globs
refsection.para: A glob is a file or path that may contain the wildcards “*” or “**/”.
The “*” wildcard matches any number of characters except “/”.
The “**/” wildcard matches any number of path segments (including none).
If a glob begins with “/”, it is anchored at the root. (Otherwise, it is logically preceded by “**/”.)
